title: Building a Neural Network Engine from First Principles in NumPy
subtitle: How to compute every gradient by hand, understand backpropagation, and achieve 97% accuracy on MNIST without PyTorch.
excerpt: The rule was simple: no autograd, no PyTorch — write matrix backprop from mathematical definitions upward.
content: When learning deep learning, it is easy to rely on frameworks like PyTorch or TensorFlow where calling `loss.backward()` hides the actual matrix calculus taking place. I wanted to understand every single line of matrix multiplication and partial derivative.
For a dense layer computing Z = W · X + b, followed by an activation A = sigmoid(Z), we use the chain rule to derive the gradient of the loss L with respect to weights W.
Implementing this in NumPy required tracking matrix shapes carefully. Batch processing with matrix products accelerated training while keeping memory footprint minimal.

1. Weight Initialization Matters: He initialization prevents vanishing gradients in deep layers.
2. Numerical Stability: Computing softmax cross-entropy loss requires subtracting max logits to avoid overflow.
3. Accuracy: Reached 97.2% on MNIST test set after 15 epochs.

title: Why I Rebuilt My Portfolio with Zero Dependencies and Pure ES Modules
subtitle: Eliminating build steps, npm bloat, and bundler overhead in favor of pure HTML5, Vanilla CSS, and native ES6 modules.
excerpt: Modern web development is bloated with build tools. Here is why building with native ES modules and zero npm packages yields superior speed and clarity.
content: Modern web development often defaults to heavy bundlers, Webpack configs, and thousands of node_modules packages. For a personal portfolio, this adds unnecessary complexity and friction.

By leveraging native browser ES modules (type='module'), each component is decoupled into clean JS modules. CSS is structured modularly with CSS Variables and backdrop-filter blur for liquid glass effects.

• Zero Build Time: Instantly loads without a compile step.
• Maximum Performance: Fast load times with zero framework overhead.
• Full Maintenance Control: Every animation and element is written from scratch.

title: HandMobile: Real-Time IMU Telemetry & Gesture Controlled Robotics
subtitle: Designing a micro-controller vehicle controlled via IMU wireless telemetry at age 14.
excerpt: Integrating hardware sensors with wireless microcontrollers to map hand gestures directly to motor PWM output in real time.
content: In 2022, I wanted to bridge hardware sensors with real-time software control. I built HandMobile — a gesture-controlled vehicle using IMU accelerometers and RF wireless modules.

The system uses an MPU-6050 6-axis gyroscope/accelerometer attached to a glove. Roll and pitch angles were processed on an Arduino and transmitted via NRF24L01 RF modules to the receiver on the vehicle.

• Sensor Filtering: Complementary filters were needed to reduce accelerometer noise.
• Latency: Low-latency serial protocols are essential for smooth real-time control.
